name: Louisiana

sources.title: Louisiana DOR -- R-1306 (1/25) Louisiana Withholding Tables and Formulas, effective on or after January 1, 2025
sources.quote: Formulas - Based on a 3.09% Withholding Rate ... 2. Single Individual and Married-Separate W = (S - (12,500/N))*.0309 3. Married-Joint Return, Qualified Surviving Spouse, or Head of Household W = (S - (25,000/N))*.0309 ... Example 1: ... $700 weekly ... =14.20

sources.title: U.S. Department of Labor, ETA -- Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective January 2025

flatRateBlockADeduction.$comment: R-1306's own Computer Formula Method, verbatim: W = (S - (deduction/N)) * .0309. The deduction is selected ENTIRELY by the employee's own Form L-4 Block A claim (0/1/2) -- genuinely different from every other status-deduction state in this project, where the deduction tier is inferred from filingStatus. Louisiana's own form explicitly allows a married employee to choose claim 0 or 1 for reasons unrelated to actual marital status (avoiding under-withholding with multiple jobs/working spouse) -- so this engine reads certificate.louisianaBlockA (0|1|2) directly rather than certificate.filingStatus.
flatRateBlockADeduction.noStandardDeductionNote: R-1306's own Formula 1 ('No Standard Deduction: W = S * .0309') is Block A claim 0 -- the default for an employee who files no certificate at all, per Form L-4's own explicit instruction.
flatRateBlockADeduction.annualizeMultiplierComment: REAL BUG CAUGHT during a 'verify' pass (2026-08-22), fixed before this ever shipped as a silent wrong-money gap: R-1306's own 'Number of Pay Periods in a year' table states 'Daily payroll: 365' -- this engine's generic PERIODS_PER_YEAR uses 260 (standard workdays) for 'daily' everywhere else, the same mismatch NJ's and Delaware's own daily tables required a dedicated override for. louisianaWithholding() now reads this map directly instead of ctx.periodsPerYear, and throws for quarterly/semiannual (not published by R-1306) rather than guessing a divisor.

roundingComment: R-1306's own worked examples are cent-precision ($13.98, $111.54) -- no whole-dollar rounding step anywhere in the document. roundHalfUp (cent-level) only.
exemptPretaxComment: Confirmed via LA R.S. 47:293's own text: Louisiana 'tax table income' for residents starts from federal adjusted gross income. Since 401(k)/125/HSA/FSA elective deferrals are excluded from federal AGI before it's ever computed, this is the same one-inferential-step-removed conformity tier as Virginia's/West Virginia's FAGI-conformity citations elsewhere in this project -- not an itemized IRC-section list the way Kentucky's/Arkansas's citations are.

additionalOrReducedWithholding.rule: Form L-4's own Line 7 is a SINGLE SIGNED adjustment field (positive to increase, negative to decrease, floored at $0 total withheld) -- the mirror of Connecticut's separate Line 2 (additional) / Line 3 (reduced) mechanic, combined into one line here. Already covered generically: a positive Line 7 value maps to certificate.additionalWithholding, a negative Line 7 value (as a positive magnitude) maps to certificate.reducedWithholding -- both are applied automatically by every state's shared pipeline (applyAdditionalStateWithholding()/applyReducedStateWithholding() in state.ts), zero new code needed.
additionalOrReducedWithholding.confidence: primary_source_confirmed -- read directly off Form L-4 itself.

reciprocity.$comment: CHECKED, not assumed absent: R-1306's full text was searched for 'reciprocal'/'reciprocity' and returned zero matches; cross-confirmed via search synthesis (multiple independent sources agree Louisiana has no reciprocal withholding agreement with any state). A Louisiana resident working in another state must file a nonresident return there and claim a Louisiana return-level credit for tax paid -- the ordinary non-reciprocal baseline every other no-reciprocity state in this project follows.

localIncomeTax.rule: NONE. No Louisiana parish or municipality levies a local income/wage tax requiring payroll withholding -- confirmed across R-1306 (zero mentions) and cross-source search synthesis.
localIncomeTax.confidence: cross_source_confirmed; not independently verified against a parish-authority statute this pass.

paidFamilyMedicalLeave.rule: NONE. No Louisiana state-run mandatory paid family/medical leave program exists as of 2026.
paidFamilyMedicalLeave.confidence: cross_source_confirmed via search synthesis, not independently fetched from a Louisiana statute this pass.

knownGaps: Descriptive notes carried from the 2026 file (reciprocity, local-tax rules, method comments) were checked against the 2025 source for the fields this engine computes from; narrative text that only describes 2026 history should be read as background.

suiEmployer.$comment: Normalized employer-side unemployment parameters — the shape src/taxes/state.ts reads. The detailed unemploymentInsurance block above stays the record of research; this exists because that block's shape varies too much between states to compute from directly (wage bases as objects, industry-keyed rate maps, differently-named keys).
suiEmployer.wageBaseSource: DOL Significant Provisions, January 2025 (Wages Subject to Tax)
suiEmployer.newEmployerRateSource: No single new-employer figure exists for this state: the rate is industry-assigned or schedule-driven. The engine therefore requires the employer's own assigned rate here and computes nothing without it.

$yearNote: 2025 ruleset: the first year of Louisiana's flat tax (Act 11 of the 2024 3rd Extraordinary Session). 3.09% withholding rate after $12,500 (Block A '1') or $25,000 (Block A '2'); 2026 indexes these to $12,875 / $25,750.
